A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the TPN solution used in this study, either given enterally or parentally, caused significant decreases in the number of cells in the PPs, LP, and IE spaces, with a concomitant decrease in IgA levels.
the administration of TPN, whether enterally or parentally, is associated with significant changes in the GALT.
TPN, either enterally administered or given intravenously, has significant adverse effects on gut-associated lymphocytes and on the IgA content of intestinal secretions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
enteral nutrition is better than parenteral nutrition.
the use of parenteral nutrition (PN) in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is not associated with increased risk of infection or death.
enteral nutrition is superior to parenteral nutrition for maintaining the integrity of the intestinal immune system.
